candidates.title: [Bugfix][Anthropic] /v1/messages drops the system prompt when the billing header shares its text block
candidates.snippet: ## Overview  `/v1/messages` strips Claude Code's `x-anthropic-billing-header: ...` line so the per-request `cch` hash does not break prefix caching. The converter currently treats "text starts with the header" as "this whole text block is the header", so when the header shares a block/string with the real system prompt, the prompt is silently dropped before the request reaches the model. candidates.title: Fixed 30 s GPU bootstrap discovery timeout silently falls back to CPU when libraries are cold on a network filesystem
candidates.snippet: ### What is the issue?  On a cluster node where the Ollama install lives on a network filesystem (Lustre), the first `ollama serve` after the libraries fall out of the page cache hits the fixed 30 s bootstrap discovery timeout in `discover/runner.go`. candidates.title: `max_tokens: 0` on `/v1/completions` generates text instead of returning an empty completion
candidates.snippet: ## What is the issue?  A `POST /v1/completions` request with `max_tokens: 0` returns HTTP 200 with 10 generated tokens. The same prompt with `max_tokens: 1` and `max_tokens: 2` returns exactly 1 and 2 tokens. Streaming behaves the same: `max_tokens: 0` emits 1 text chunk instead of an empty response.  **Affected version:** `>= v0.2.0` (`/v1/completions` route added in `d626b99b5`, first stable tag v0.2.0). candidates.title: Manifest fetch for a large model stays stuck across dozens of client retries; only a server restart unblocks it
candidates.snippet: Ollama 0.40.17 on Ubuntu 26.04 (WSL2), pulling mdq100/qwen3.5-coder:35b (23 GB blob set). `ollama pull` printed "pulling manifest" and never progressed. I restarted the pull client dozens of times over several hours; every attempt stuck at the same place. No network error was shown and the registry was reachable. `sudo systemctl restart ollama` (server restart) immediately unblocked the manifest fetch and the pull proceeded.
